tagline: Soviet Venus + Halley's Comet double mission — Venera lander, first interplanetary balloon, then Halley flyby
description: First spacecraft of the international Halley armada. Launched 1984-12-15 on a Proton-K / D-1. The 4920 kg flyby bus carried a ~1500 kg descent module that separated for Venus arrival 1985-06-11 — the lander touched down at 7.5°N, 177.8°E for 56 minutes of surface science, while a first-of-kind helium-filled balloon aerostat floated in the cloud deck at 54 km altitude for 46 hours tracking wind speeds and atmospheric structure. The flyby bus continued on its 9-month cruise and encountered comet 1P/Halley 1986-03-06 at 8889 km — the first Halley encounter of the armada, providing the targeting data ESA's Giotto used 8 days later for its much closer 596 km approach.
best_known_for: Soviet Venus + Halley double mission — first interplanetary balloon, first Halley flyby
